speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you are experiencing sudden-onset vertigo; to help me pinpoint the cause, I need to know exactly what you mean by "sudden-onset"—did this happen at a specific moment, or did it develop gradually over hours? Additionally, have you experienced any nausea, hearing loss, or ringing in your ears alongside the spinning sensation?

speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with a sudden-onset sensation that the room is spinning, leading to several episodes of nausea and vomiting. The symptoms started as he was going to bed and lasted for approximately 3 minutes. He mentions that he has never experienced anything like this before and currently feels at his baseline.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV).

The brief duration of your symptoms (3 minutes), sudden onset while lying down, and current return to baseline are classic signs of BPPV. Since you feel better now and have no hearing loss, I do not require further imaging or hearing tests at this time. I will perform a Dix-Hallpike maneuver to confirm the diagnosis and treat the affected canal.
